questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Sudan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Sudan article.

questions.proof: Its capital and largest city is Khartoum.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Sudan?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Sudan on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Sudan article.

questions.proof: Sudan borders Egypt to the north, Eritrea and Ethiopia to the east, South Sudan to the south, the Central African Republic to the southwest, Chad to the west, and Libya to the northwest.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Sudan?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Culture” part of the Sudan article.

questions.proof: Arabic is the official language of Sudan.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Sudan?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Culture” part of the Sudan article.

questions.proof: The currency of Sudan is called the Sudanese Pound (SDG) (Jinneh Sudani).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “However, on 9 July _____, the southern part of the country separated and became a new country, South Sudan.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Sudan article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: However, on 9 July 2011, the southern part of the country separated and became a new country, South Sudan.
